prompt: A vast dim warehouse of specialised workshop stalls—each a distinct expert with its own tools and signage—stands mostly shuttered and gathering dust, while a central router like a railway switchman inspects an incoming word-token and throws only a few levers so that a tiny glowing team of stalls lights up and processes it; a towering billboard boasts the sum of every stall’s parameters as a colossal total, yet a modest energy meter beside the active stalls shows the per-token cost of a far smaller dense network, unused stalls visibly wasting floor space, and the entire unused inventory still occupying a cavernous memory vault in the background, with a faded archival plaque noting that this sparse-routing idea predates today’s chat models and became the standard way to scale language networks past the expense of keeping every neuron awake.
